pages.en:
There is a sound.

The door of the shed opening: old, badly fitted, its hinges rusted, heavier than it has any right to be.

pages.ja:
暗かった土蔵に光が差し込んでくる。
「
」
意識が眠りから覚めていく。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Light spills into the dark shed.

“…”

Sleep begins to loosen its hold on me.

pages.ja:
「先輩、起きてますか？」
近づいてくる足音が誰なのかは、確かめるまでもない。
ああ、もうそんな時間なのか。
ほう、と息をついて目蓋を開けた。

pages.en:
“Are you awake?”

I don’t need to look to know whose footsteps are approaching.

Oh. That time already.

I let out a long breath and open my eyes.

pages.ja:
「おはようございます先輩。そろそろ時間ですよ」
「ん
そうみたいだ。おはよう桜。起こしにきてくれてサンキューな」
pages.jaRuby:
「おはようございます先輩。そろそろ時間ですよ」
「ん
そうみたいだ。おはよう桜。起こしにきてくれてサンキューな」
pages.en:
“Good morning. It’s almost time, you know.”

“Mm… Looks like it. Morning, Sakura. Thanks for coming to wake me.”

pages.ja: 「いえ、お礼を言われる事じゃありません。先輩ならきちんと起きてくれるって判ってましたから、わたしは余計な事をしただけなんです」
pages.jaRuby: 「いえ、お礼を言われる事じゃありません。先輩ならきちんと起きてくれるって判ってましたから、わたしは余計な事をしただけなんです」
pages.en: “Oh, you don’t have to thank me. I knew you’d get up properly on your own. I just came and made myself unnecessary.”

pages.ja:
「そっか。……けど、ならなんでわざわざ起こしに来てくれたんだ？」
「わざわざじゃありません。今朝は先輩を起こしたくなって、いつもより三十分も早起きしたんです。今日は特別な日ですから」
pages.jaRuby:
「そっか。……けど、ならなんでわざわざ起こしに来てくれたんだ？」
「わざわざじゃありません。今朝は先輩を起こしたくなって、いつもより三十分も早起きしたんです。今日は特別な日ですから」
pages.en:
“Right. …But then why go to the trouble of waking me?”

“It wasn’t any trouble. This morning I wanted to wake you, so I got up a whole half hour early. Today’s a special day.”

pages.ja:
「
あ」
それで気が付いた。
そうだ。今日は特別な日だったんだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「
あ」

pages.en:
“—Oh.”

Now I remember.

She’s right. Today is special.

「桜。訊くまでもないと思うんだが、藤ねえはまだ来てないよな？」
「はい、藤村先生はまだ。あ、でもイリヤちゃんは先に来てます」
pages.jaRuby:
「桜。訊くまでもないと思うんだが、藤ねえはまだ来てないよな？」
「はい、藤村先生はまだ。あ、でもイリヤちゃんは先に来てます」
pages.en:
“Sakura. I probably don’t need to ask, but Taiga isn’t here yet, is she?”

“No, Miss Fujimura hasn’t arrived. Oh, but Illya’s already here.”

pages.ja:
やっぱり。
イリヤだけ来ているというコトは、つまりはそういうコトなのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
やっぱり。
イリヤだけ来ているというコトは、つまりはそういうコトなのだ。
pages.en:
I thought so.

If Illya’s come on her own, that can only mean one thing.

「
まずい。桜、すまないんだけど朝食の支度を頼む。俺、ひとっ走りして藤ねえをたたき起こしてくる」
「あ、はい。ごくろうさまです、先輩」

pages.en:
“—Not good. Sorry, Sakura, but can I leave breakfast to you? I’ll run over and haul Taiga out of bed.”

“Oh—yes. Good luck.”

幸い、昨夜も遅くまで作業していたんで作業服のままだ。
着替えなくとも外に飛び出せるのは有り難い。

着替えなくとも外に飛び出せるのは有り難い。
pages.en:
Fortunately, I was working late again last night, so I’m still in my work clothes.

At least I can rush straight out without having to change.

pages.ja:
「十分で戻るから、後はよろしく頼む」
「はい、まかせちゃってください」
pages.jaRuby:
「十分で戻るから、後はよろしく頼む」
「はい、まかせちゃってください」
pages.en:
“I’ll be back in ten minutes. Hold the fort for me.”

“Yes! Leave it to me.”

pages.ja:
「あれ、シロウ起きてる」
「ああ、いま起きた。ちょっと藤ねえ起こしてくるから、桜の手伝いをしてやってくれ」
ぽん、とイリヤの肩に手を置いて、そのまま玄関へ向かっていく。

pages.en:
“Oh. You’re awake, Shirou.”

“Yeah, just got up. I’m off to wake Taiga. Give Sakura a hand, will you?”

I pat Illya’s shoulder and keep going toward the front door.

「
やられた。もう、シロウはわたしが起こしに行くって言ったでしょ、サクラー！」
イリヤは怒鳴りながら土蔵へ走っていく。
そんな光景も、今ではそう珍しくない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“—She beat me to it. Sakura! I *told* you I was going to wake Shirou!”

Illya runs off toward the shed, shouting.

These days, it’s hardly an unusual sight.

pages.ja:
イリヤが国には帰らないと言いだしたんで、ならうちで預かろうと藤ねえに相談した。
藤ねえは猛反対しつつ、それなら藤村のうちのがいい、とイリヤを預かってくれたのだ。
以来、イリヤは藤村の家で居候しながら、藤ねえと一緒に朝夕と襲撃にくる。
言うまでもなく、狙いは朝飯と晩飯だ。
同居を初めて二ヶ月、二人は既に一心同体っぽい。

pages.en:
When Illya announced that she wasn’t going home to her own country, I asked Taiga whether she could stay with us.

Taiga objected fiercely, then offered to take her in herself: if that was how things stood, she said, the Fujimura house would be much better.

Ever since, Illya has been living there and joining Taiga in twice-daily raids on our house.

Needless to say, their targets are breakfast and dinner.

Two months under the same roof, and they’re practically joined at the hip.

pages.ja:
土蔵の裏側を通りかかると、塀の向こうから声が聞こえてきた。
桜とイリヤの話し声だ。

pages.en:
As I pass behind the shed, I hear voices from the other side of the wall.

Sakura and Illya.

でこぼこコンビというか、きびきびしたイリヤとのんびりした桜は、騒がしいながらも仲がいいみたいだ。
実際、イリヤのおかげで桜は元気を取り戻しつつある。

pages.en:
With Illya’s complete lack of restraint, I’d thought she and Sakura wouldn’t get along. Apparently I was wrong.

A bit of an odd couple, maybe—brisk, lively Illya and easygoing Sakura—but for all the noise, they seem to be good friends.

In fact, thanks to Illya, Sakura is starting to find her feet again.

pages.ja:

例の学校での集団昏睡事件との関わりを、桜も薄々感じていたのだろう。
桜は行方の知れない慎二を気に病んで、長いこと塞ぎ込んでいた。

…After her brother Shinji Matou disappeared and was officially listed as missing, Sakura stopped smiling.

She must have had some inkling that his disappearance was connected to the incident at school, when everyone fell unconscious.

Worrying about her missing brother, she withdrew into herself for a long time.

「
うん。桜、笑えるようになったよな」

やっぱり桜には、ああいうふんわりとした笑顔が似合うんだから。

It was Illya who dragged her out again by sheer force. When Illya is around, some of Sakura’s brightness returns.

“—Yeah. She can smile again.”

That makes me happy, quite simply.

That soft smile suits her so well.

「うう、酷いよぅイリヤちゃん。何があっても起こしてって臨時ボーナスまであげたのにあげたのに」
よよよ、と泣き崩れながら朝食をかっこむ藤ねえ。

pages.en:
“Ugh… You’re so mean, Illya. I even gave you a special bonus to make sure you woke me, no matter what. A bonus! I gave you a bonus!”

Taiga shovels down her breakfast through a performance of heartbroken sobbing.

pages.ja: 「当然よ。タイガを待ってたらわたしまで遅れるし、給金分は義理を果たしたわ。あれ以上の働きを要求するなら、臨時じゃなくて基本給をアップさせるコトね」

pages.en: “Of course I left. If I’d waited for you, I’d have been late too. I did what you paid me for. If you want more work than that, raise my regular pay instead of handing out bonuses.”

pages.ja:
「……むむ。わたしだけじゃなくお爺さまからも貰ってるクセに、どうしてこうこの子は守銭奴なのかしら。
若い頃からお金にうるさいとまわりの子に嫌われちゃうぞー」

pages.en:
“…Hmph. It’s not just me paying you. You get money from Grandfather too. How did you turn into such a little miser?

“Keep fussing over money at your age and the other children won’t like you.”

pages.ja: 「嫌われて結構よ。好きな人以外なら何を思われても関係ないもの。それよりタイガ、貸したお金ちゃんと返してよね。給料日、五日前だったんでしょ」

pages.en: “They’re welcome not to. I don’t care what anyone thinks unless I like them. More importantly, Taiga, you’d better pay back the money I lent you. Payday was five days ago, wasn’t it?”

pages.ja:
「
え。な、なんでそんなコト知ってるのよあなた！」
「ライガに聞いたわ。お望みなら明細まで話してあげてよ」
pages.jaRuby:
「

「ライガに聞いたわ。お望みなら明細まで話してあげてよ」
pages.en:
“—What? H-how do you know that?”

“I asked Raiga. I can go through your payslip too, if you like.”

加えて、イリヤは藤ねえ相手だととんでもなく意地悪になる。今の笑い方なんてどこかの誰かさんそっくりだし。

Illya gives her a fearless little grin.

Unlike Sakura, Taiga is just about the worst possible match for her.

And Illya gets unbelievably nasty when Taiga is involved. That smile just now could have belonged to a certain someone else.

「返済は明日までね。出来なかったらタイガのおこづかいから引いていくから」
「……！ お、お爺さま、そんなコトまであなたに話したの！？」

pages.en:
“You have until tomorrow. If you can’t pay me back, I’ll have it taken out of your allowance.”

“…! G-Grandfather told you about *that*?”

“Yes. We spend all afternoon together. He told me I was much cuter than you.”

“Aaah…! Do something, Shirou! You’ve brought home a little devil! At this rate she’ll take over the Fujimura clan!”

“…”

Wait. Forget that for a moment.

At your age, you’re still getting an allowance from your grandfather…?

「ん、努力する。留守番よろしくな、イリヤ」

pages.en:
“Have a good day, Shirou. You’re finishing early, aren’t you? I’ll wait here, then. Come straight home.”

“Mm. I’ll do my best. Look after the house for me, Illya.”

Taiga sulks from behind my back.

“Yes, yes. You be good too, Taiga. Don’t go making trouble for Shirou while you’re out.”

Illya brushes her off without an effort.

The balance of power seems to have shifted well beyond anything Taiga can hope to overturn.

“I’m going ahead, Shirou. Don’t dawdle and make yourself late!”

With a sputtering roar that rises to a shriek, Taiga shoots away like a bullet.

She got her license a month ago.

Since then, the number of times she’s been late has fallen spectacularly. She’s also acquired a new nickname: Rocket Tiger—or rather, Rocket Diver.

She’s the only one who doesn’t know.

桜は一足先に登校している。
ごはんを大盛りにしていたところを見ると、たいそう気合いが入っているようだった。

I stretch my back and take a deep breath.

Sakura has already left for school.

Judging by the mountain of rice she ate, she’s taking today very seriously.

It’s the archery club’s make-or-break day. As vice-captain, she must be determined to do her part.

“—Right, then.”

Off to school.

It’s April seventh.

Today is the entrance ceremony. The cold winter has passed, and spring is here.

彼女がいなくなってから随分と変わった気がするが、変化なんて些細なものなのだと思う。

pages.en:
Two months since then.

It feels as though so much has changed since she left. But I think the changes themselves are small.

Winter ended. Spring came.

That’s all that changed.

I may feel as though I’ve grown a little, but that doesn’t mean I’ve become someone you wouldn’t recognize.

So very little has changed, really.

Shirou Emiya is still running clumsily after Kiritsugu.

“Well, sure, we never used to bump into each other this often.”

単刀直入に訊いた。

“Tohsaka. Aren’t you sleepy?”

I ask her outright.

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…What’s that supposed to mean? I’m not sleepy, and I’m not pushing myself.

“Why would you even ask me that?”

Something along the lines of *Who dares disturb my slumber? I’ll kill you.*

“I-I would do no such thing! Getting up half an hour early isn’t enough to catch me off guard!”

“There. You *have* been getting up early.”

風は心地よく、時折、高台にある校舎から桜の葉が舞い散ってくる。

We climb the hill.

The town spread below us has taken on the look of spring.

The wind feels good. Now and then, cherry leaves drift down from the school on the hilltop.

Everything I see, everything I feel against my skin, makes me want to smile.

The person who understands Illya best isn’t Sakura or me. It’s Tohsaka.

Partly because she checks on Illya’s health regularly, but more than anything because they’re both magi to the bone.

Illya still hasn’t quite grasped what it means to live with her magecraft hidden. I think Tohsaka will make a good teacher.

Two months have passed—and only now, for the first time, have we spoken of the girl with golden hair.

“It happens. Sometimes a person fulfills their life’s ambition by some mistake, and just like that, they drop dead.

Maybe she means dying content, or finally finding peace.

“So yes, I was worried. At a time like that, everyone around you feels much safer if you fall apart spectacularly.”

“What, you’d have comforted me if I’d been depressed?”

Tohsaka murmurs it without looking away from the sky.

Everything was there in that farewell.

What I wanted to do.

What she dreamed of.

Perhaps we were just being stubborn with each other. Perhaps I should have taken her hand and made that girl’s dream come true.

There is nothing to regret.

She brought her own time to its proper close.

I can’t stay here inside this memory, either.

Grumbling, I sling my bag over my shoulder and start running.

It’s only seven thirty.

Far too early for lazy students who aren’t in any clubs. Still, I suppose there’s no harm in getting there early.

Today marks the start of a new year.

If I’m going to welcome it, I have to shake off old memories and hurry on.

However hard they are to leave.

Even if the emptiness that strikes my heart brings me close to tears.

If I keep my eyes on something far away, perhaps one day my hand will reach what I’ve been striving for.

Winter is over. A new spring begins.

I climb the hill beneath a blue sky she, too, must once have seen.

The battle was over.

Her last battlefield. The war that had split the country in two had ended in the king’s victory.

Curses filled the hill buried beneath the dead. Their bitter cries called for the living to follow them.

A bridle was clenched in his hand. A wounded white horse struggled to keep up.

The knight and the horse were all that remained alive.

And one king, slumped across the horse’s back.

The king he served was in death’s grasp.

He had defeated the enemy king in single combat, but had himself suffered a mortal wound.

Even the knight could see there was no hope of healing it.

The king they had served would soon die.

That their king was eternal.

That so long as the holy sword guided him, their king could never perish.

Isolated at court. Resented by the knights. Feared by the people.

Even in that plight, the young king had shown no private feeling and remained an ideal. The knight was proud of him for it.

He had pledged his sword because it was *this* king. He had striven to be of use, and despite his youth had risen to serve in the royal guard.

A king whose true face could not be seen.

A boy who set personal feeling aside and sought to be fair, to be selfless.

Perhaps, the knight had hoped, if he could get close enough, he would see the king’s true face.

Not the face the king wore in the castle or on the battlefield, but an unguarded face. The smile of a human being.

Surely it would appear somewhere within the court, when the king was free of his duties.

Even a perfect king could not remain vigilant every moment of the day.

He wanted to believe such a thing must not be allowed.

Forgive me, he thought. This will be my first and last deception of my king.

His face remained lowered. He did not look up at the knight.

His breathing was so faint it could scarcely be discerned. Quietly—

In a voice worn thin, the king gave his final command.

To defy his king was, for a knight, a grievous sin.
